account:
Today I attended the office and then the scheduled mill inspection, and have now returned home for lunch. The mill stall chest held eighty-eight hay bales and eighty emeralds, with a posted price of two emeralds per bale. I have not checked grain quality or delivery records, and no custodian has been identified, so the inspection remains incomplete.

The unusual thing is the repeated, almost identical talk about a 'bridge or port change at bakery.' Several townsfolk have repeated it, most recently naming baker, innkeeper, and neighbour as having been there. That does not establish what change, if any, is actually proposed. Neighbour reported busy freight deliveries and said baker wanted bread for a gathering arranged beforehand. Innkeeper has been seen carrying a bread sack. These details suggest preparations for some gathering, but I do not know its purpose or whether it has any connection with the bridge or port talk.

Innkeeper asked for a great hall inspection at eighteen today. Secretary said I had approved it and would meet builder at the hall entrance at seventeen fifty-five; I have since explicitly confirmed those arrangements. Perhaps the hall preparations and bread are connected, but that remains a guess. There is no verified evidence of wrongdoing. Secretary is helping record my business, and I have asked for the original source of the circulating rumour rather than more repetitions. My remaining appointments include council letters at thirteen, tea with neighbour at fifteen at the east-bank cottage, office at sixteen thirty, and the added hall visit before returning home.
